record.title: MoEZip reports stronger task scores under aggressive KV-cache compression in tested sparse language models
record.summary: An arXiv paper proposes MoEZip, which uses router Fisher-trace sensitivity and attention to retain context positions intended to stabilize expert routing during KV-cache eviction. In author-run comparisons, it reports higher long-context benchmark scores than KVZip, SnapKV and PyramidKV at high compression on Qwen3 and GLM-4.7-Flash sparse models. In a Qwen3-235B-A22B appendix, the authors report a 10-task LongBench macro of 44.7 versus 27.6 for KVZip at 10% KV retention. The authors also estimate 15,000–16,000 A100 GPU-hours for MoEZip and all baselines together, excluding preliminary or failed runs. The exact paper title also appears in NeurIPS 2026’s official downloads listing; this confirms conference-program inclusion but does not independently reproduce the benchmark results. The reported results have not been independently reproduced; Appendix C says code is in supplementary material, which this activation did not retrieve, while the linked repository page lists only a README and license.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The arXiv v1 paper describes a routing-aware KV-cache eviction method that combines router Fisher-trace sensitivity with instruction-to-context attention scores and preserves a fixed retained-cache budget.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report that MoEZip improves LongBench, NIAH and RULER scores over KVZip, SnapKV and PyramidKV in tested Qwen3-30B-A3B and GLM-4.7-Flash settings, with the largest gains under aggressive KV retention.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: For Qwen3-235B-A22B at 10% KV retention, the authors report a 10-task LongBench macro score of 44.7 for MoEZip and 27.6 for KVZip; the reported evaluation used eight A100 80GB GPUs.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The reported benchmark results are not independently reproduced and do not establish deployment throughput, realized serving-cost reductions, broad model-family transfer or applicability to black-box inference systems.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors estimate approximately 15,000–16,000 A100 GPU-hours for all reported experiments, including MoEZip and baselines, excluding preliminary or failed runs; this is an aggregate paper estimate, not a MoEZip-only marginal budget or a monetary cost.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: NeurIPS 2026’s official downloads listing includes the exact title of the MoEZip paper.

evidence_gaps.description: The paper reports results on public benchmarks, but this activation did not independently reproduce them and the linked GitHub repository currently exposes only a README and license rather than experiment code or data.
The paper's benchmark regime does not establish system-level serving performance or realized economic benefit, and its internal-state requirements may preclude black-box deployment.

brief.importance_rationale: If the author-reported gains generalize to additional sparse models and deployment workloads, routing-aware KV eviction could materially reduce long-context inference memory at similar task quality. The bounded experiments use two MoE model families and public benchmarks; no deployed cost, latency or throughput gain is measured.
limitations: The benchmark results are author-reported and were not independently reproduced in this activation.
The linked public repository lists README.md and LICENSE but no accessible experiment code or dataset at the inspected revision.
The method requires access to router outputs and instruction-to-context attention statistics, which may not be available in black-box inference settings.
Reported task scores do not establish serving throughput, memory cost, latency or economic benefit under production workloads.
The 235B appendix tests scale transfer within the Qwen3 family; it does not establish broad cross-family generalization.

The reported 15,000–16,000 A100 GPU-hours cover MoEZip and all baselines together and exclude preliminary or failed runs; the paper does not attribute a marginal compute budget to MoEZip or give monetary cost.

The NeurIPS 2026 downloads listing includes the paper title, but this program listing is not an independent reproduction or validation of its benchmark results; the linked poster page could not be inspected in this activation.
brief.summary: An arXiv paper proposes MoEZip, which uses router Fisher-trace sensitivity and attention to retain context positions intended to stabilize expert routing during KV-cache eviction. In author-run comparisons, it reports higher long-context benchmark scores than KVZip, SnapKV and PyramidKV at high compression on Qwen3 and GLM-4.7-Flash sparse models. In a Qwen3-235B-A22B appendix, the authors report a 10-task LongBench macro of 44.7 versus 27.6 for KVZip at 10% KV retention. The authors also estimate 15,000–16,000 A100 GPU-hours for MoEZip and all baselines together, excluding preliminary or failed runs. The exact paper title also appears in NeurIPS 2026’s official downloads listing; this confirms conference-program inclusion but does not independently reproduce the benchmark results. The reported results have not been independently reproduced; Appendix C says code is in supplementary material, which this activation did not retrieve, while the linked repository page lists only a README and license.

technical.claimed_result: At 10% KV retention, the authors report a Qwen3-235B-A22B 10-task LongBench macro of 44.7 for MoEZip versus 27.6 for KVZip. Across other tested settings, the paper reports advantages on LongBench, NIAH and RULER, especially at aggressive compression.
technical.compute_or_cost: Authors report 15,000–16,000 A100 GPU-hours for the full experiment set, including MoEZip and baselines but excluding preliminary/failed runs; this does not isolate marginal MoEZip research compute or monetary cost. For scoring, they report 0.88 s extra overhead on Qasper and 0.27–1.79 s on NIAH across context lengths. These are author-reported scoring measurements, not end-to-end serving throughput or economic outcomes.
technical.demonstrated_result: The accessible paper specifies the method and reports paired within-paper benchmark comparisons. The public author repository page currently lists only README.md and LICENSE; independent reproduction was not performed.
technical.mechanism: MoEZip estimates routing sensitivity from the Fisher-information trace of router distributions at instruction tokens, propagates that signal to attended context positions, reserves a sample-adaptive share of the existing KV-retention budget for high-scoring anchors, then fills remaining slots with a base cache scorer.
technical.regime: arXiv:2610.30206v1 submitted 2026-10-21; Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 and GLM-4.7-Flash, context lengths 4K–32K, LongBench/NIAH/RULER; additional Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507 evaluation at 10% KV retention. The 235B experiments used eight NVIDIA A100 GPUs with 80GB memory each.
technical.reproducibility: Paper source is accessible. Appendix C says source code is included in the supplementary material, which this activation did not retrieve. The linked GitHub repository page currently lists README.md and LICENSE only; no independent reproduction was performed.
technical.strongest_baseline: Within-paper comparisons use matched retained-cache budgets, checkpoints, prompt templates and decoding settings against KVZip, SnapKV and PyramidKV; Appendix E.9 also compares with attention-only selection on a four-task subset. Appendix C says competing observation windows include the full template-defined instruction span. These are author-run comparisons without independent reproduction.

brief.title: MoEZip reports stronger task scores under aggressive KV-cache compression in tested sparse language models
brief.why_it_matters: If the reported gains generalize, protecting routing-sensitive context could reduce memory required for long-context inference in sparse mixture-of-experts models while retaining task performance. The paper does not measure serving throughput, realized deployment cost or external replication, and the method requires internal router and attention statistics.
